method: Independent conservative DXF evidence audit. Safe binding requires explicit semantic/reference evidence; unresolved wall-face candidates are reported separately and never promoted to engineering truth.
interpretation: All six files reproduce the protected v1 aggregate counts exactly: 835 total, 810 linear/rotated, 25 aligned, 34 explicit overrides, 16 numeric overrides, 18 non-numeric overrides, 7 zero-measurement dimensions.
All six declare $INSUNITS=4 while dimension plausibility resolves effective metre units with high confidence; header metadata cannot be sole numeric authority.

Safe semantic binding varies from 0% to 97.7%, proving that imported drafting conventions are heterogeneous and that a production engine must not infer semantic certainty from recurrence, layer names or visual proximity alone.

Including unresolved wall candidates raises aggregate potential binding only from 50.7% to 63.5%; wall reference basis and ambiguous geometry therefore remain legitimate human checkpoints rather than defects to hide with heuristics.
Per-file semantic-class labels from the audit are diagnostic only and are intentionally not stored as generation rules because raw layer vocabulary can be misleading.
promotion_effect: Benchmark supports shadow-first v2 and fail-closed human review. It does not authorize visible-output promotion or any benchmark-derived engineering default.
